sections.subtitle: Real Conditions: Si + Present Indicative
sections.content: REAL CONDITIONS express situations that are likely, possible, or habitual. Use SI + PRESENT INDICATIVE in the condition clause, and PRESENT or FUTURE in the result clause. Pattern: Si + present, present/future/imperative. Examples with PRESENT result: 'Si llueve, no voy' (If it rains, I don't go - habitual). 'Si tengo tiempo, leo' (If I have time, I read - regular occurrence). Examples with FUTURE result: 'Si llueve, no iré' (If it rains, I won't go - future possibility). 'Si estudias, aprobarás' (If you study, you'll pass - likely future). Examples with IMPERATIVE: 'Si ves a Juan, dile hola' (If you see Juan, say hello to him - command). These express OPEN CONDITIONS - situations that may actually happen. The condition is presented as realistic and possible. Note: Never use future tense after SI in Spanish, even when referring to future. WRONG: 'Si lloverá...' CORRECT: 'Si llueve...' (present tense even for future meaning).

sections.subtitle: Future Possibilities & Real Condition Nuances
sections.content: FUTURE POSSIBILITIES in result clause: When the condition is likely/possible, use future tense in the result. 'Si hace buen tiempo, iremos a la playa' (If the weather is good, we'll go to the beach). 'Si terminas temprano, podremos cenar juntos' (If you finish early, we'll be able to have dinner together). The present tense in SI clause + future in result clause is extremely common for real future conditions. PRESENT in result: Express habitual actions or general truths. 'Si como mucho, me siento mal' (If I eat a lot, I feel bad - always happens). 'Si el agua llega a 100°, hierve' (If water reaches 100°, it boils - universal truth). IMPERATIVE in result: Give commands or instructions based on conditions. 'Si tienes frío, ponte un suéter' (If you're cold, put on a sweater). 'Si no entiendes, pregunta' (If you don't understand, ask). Remember: All these use INDICATIVE (not subjunctive) in the SI clause because they express real, open possibilities.

sections.subtitle: Hypothetical Present: Si + Imperfect Subjunctive
sections.content: HYPOTHETICAL CONDITIONS express contrary-to-fact or unlikely situations in the present/future. Pattern: SI + IMPERFECT SUBJUNCTIVE, CONDITIONAL. The imperfect subjunctive signals 'this isn't real' or 'this is unlikely'. Examples: 'Si tuviera dinero, compraría un coche' (If I had money, I would buy a car - but I don't have money now). 'Si fuera rico, viajaría por el mundo' (If I were rich, I would travel the world - but I'm not rich). 'Si pudiera volar, iría a la luna' (If I could fly, I would go to the moon - impossible/contrary to reality). The CONDITIONAL in the result clause expresses what WOULD happen in the hypothetical scenario. More examples: 'Si hablara chino, conseguiría ese trabajo' (If I spoke Chinese, I would get that job - but I don't speak Chinese). 'Si vivieras más cerca, te visitaría más' (If you lived closer, I would visit you more - but you don't live close). Common verbs in imperfect subjunctive: tuviera/tuviese (had), fuera/fuese (were), pudiera/pudiese (could), hiciera/hiciese (did/made), supiera/supiese (knew).

sections.subtitle: Real vs Hypothetical: Key Distinctions
sections.content: Understanding the difference is crucial. REAL (present indicative): 'Si tengo tiempo, voy al cine' (If I have time, I go to the cinema - it's possible I'll have time, this happens sometimes). HYPOTHETICAL (imperfect subjunctive): 'Si tuviera tiempo, iría al cine' (If I had time, I would go to the cinema - I don't have time, contrary to current reality). REAL: 'Si Juan está aquí, puedo preguntarle' (If Juan is here, I can ask him - he might be here, let me check). HYPOTHETICAL: 'Si Juan estuviera aquí, podría preguntarle' (If Juan were here, I could ask him - but he's not here now). The hypothetical suggests impossibility, unlikelihood, or imagining a different reality. REAL: 'Si llueve mañana, no iremos' (If it rains tomorrow, we won't go - realistic possibility). HYPOTHETICAL: 'Si lloviera en el desierto, crecerían plantas' (If it rained in the desert, plants would grow - unlikely/imagining different scenario). The choice depends on how the speaker views the condition: possible reality vs imagined/contrary-to-fact scenario.

sections.subtitle: Past Hypotheticals: Si + Pluperfect Subjunctive
sections.content: PAST HYPOTHETICAL (or unreal past) conditions express situations that didn't happen in the past - 'what could have been'. Pattern: SI + PLUPERFECT SUBJUNCTIVE, CONDITIONAL PERFECT. Pluperfect subjunctive formed: hubiera/hubiese + past participle. Conditional perfect formed: habría + past participle. Examples: 'Si hubiera estudiado, habría aprobado' (If I had studied, I would have passed - but I didn't study, and I didn't pass). 'Si hubieras venido, habrías conocido a María' (If you had come, you would have met María - but you didn't come, so you didn't meet her). 'Si hubiéramos salido antes, habríamos llegado a tiempo' (If we had left earlier, we would have arrived on time - but we didn't leave earlier, so we were late). These express regret, missed opportunities, or analyzing past alternatives. More examples: 'Si lo hubiera sabido, no habría ido' (If I had known it, I wouldn't have gone - expresses regret). 'Si hubiera tenido dinero, habría comprado la casa' (If I had had money, I would have bought the house - missed opportunity). This structure is common for reflecting on past decisions and their potential outcomes.

sections.subtitle: Alternative Conditional Structures
sections.content: COMO + SUBJUNCTIVE (warning/threat): 'Como llegues tarde, te quedarás sin postre' (If you arrive late, you'll go without dessert - threat/warning). 'Como no estudies, suspenderás' (If you don't study, you'll fail - strong warning). Used for consequences/warnings, more forceful than simple si. The subjunctive here signals a hypothetical future action being warned against. DE + INFINITIVE (formal/literary): Replaces si clauses in formal writing. 'De tener tiempo, iría contigo' (If I had time, I would go with you - formal alternative to 'Si tuviera tiempo...'). 'De haberlo sabido, no habría venido' (If I had known it, I wouldn't have come - formal alternative to 'Si lo hubiera sabido...'). Generally seen in literature or formal contexts; less common in everyday speech. WITHOUT SI - implied conditions: Sometimes the condition is implied rather than stated. 'Con más dinero, viajaría más' (With more money, I would travel more - implies 'if I had more money'). 'En tu lugar, yo no iría' (In your place, I wouldn't go - implies 'if I were in your place'). Other patterns: 'A no ser que' (unless), 'En caso de que' (in case), 'Con tal de que' (provided that) - all require subjunctive and express conditions.

questions.question: What tense follows SI in real conditions?
questions.hint: Real conditions: SI + PRESENT indicative. Example: Si llueve (present), no iré.

questions.question: 'Si llueve, no iré' - Is this real or hypothetical?
questions.hint: Present indicative (llueve) = real condition. It might actually rain; this is a real possibility.

questions.question: 'Si lloverá mañana, no iré' - Is this correct?

answers.text: No - never use future after SI, use present: Si llueve
Yes - future after SI is correct
Yes - but only in formal Spanish

questions.hint: NEVER use future tense after SI. Always use present for future conditions: Si llueve (not lloverá).

questions.question: 'Si estudias, aprobarás' - What tense is 'aprobarás'?
questions.hint: Aprobarás = future tense (you will pass). Common pattern: Si + present, future.

questions.question: 'Si tengo tiempo, leo' - What does this express?

answers.text: Habitual action (whenever I have time, I read)

questions.hint: Si + present, present = habitual action. Whenever this happens, that happens.

questions.question: 'Si ves a Juan, dile hola' - What form is 'dile'?
questions.hint: Pattern: Si + present, imperative. If you see Juan, tell (command) him hello.

questions.question: What pattern expresses hypothetical present conditions?
questions.hint: Hypothetical present: Si + imperfect subjunctive, conditional. Si tuviera, compraría.

questions.question: 'Si tuviera dinero, compraría un coche' - What does this mean?

answers.text: If I had money, I would buy a car (but I don't have money)
If I have money, I will buy a car (real possibility)
If I had had money, I would have bought a car (past)
When I have money, I buy a car (habitual)

questions.hint: Imperfect subjunctive (tuviera) + conditional (compraría) = hypothetical, contrary to present reality.

questions.question: 'Si fuera rico, viajaría' - Is the speaker rich?

answers.text: Was rich in past, not now

questions.hint: Si + imperfect subjunctive = contrary to fact. If I WERE rich (but I'm NOT), I would travel.

questions.question: 'Si tengo tiempo, voy' vs 'Si tuviera tiempo, iría' - What's the difference?

answers.text: First is real possibility; second is hypothetical/I don't have time
First is past; second is present
No difference, both mean the same
First is formal; second is informal

questions.hint: TENGO = real possibility. TUVIERA = hypothetical/contrary to fact (I don't have time).

questions.question: 'Si Juan estuviera aquí, podría preguntarle' - Is Juan here?
questions.hint: Imperfect subjunctive (estuviera) = contrary to fact. If he WERE here (but he's NOT).

questions.question: 'Si pudiera volar, iría a la luna' - Can the speaker fly?

answers.text: Will be able to fly in future

questions.hint: Si pudiera (imperfect subjunctive) = hypothetical/impossible. If I COULD fly (but I can't).

questions.question: What pattern expresses past hypothetical conditions?
questions.hint: Past hypothetical: Si + pluperfect subjunctive, conditional perfect. Si hubiera estudiado, habría aprobado.

questions.question: 'Si hubiera estudiado, habría aprobado' - Did the speaker study?

answers.text: No (didn't study, didn't pass - past hypothetical)

questions.hint: Pluperfect subjunctive = didn't happen in past. If I HAD studied (but I didn't), I would have passed (but I didn't).

questions.question: 'Si hubieras venido, habrías conocido a María' - Did 'you' come?
questions.hint: Past hypothetical: If you HAD come (but you didn't), you would have met María (but you didn't).

questions.question: 'Si lo hubiera sabido, no habría ido' - What does this express?

answers.text: Regret (didn't know, went, now regrets it)

questions.hint: Past hypothetical often expresses regret. If I had known (but I didn't), I wouldn't have gone (but I did).

questions.question: How is pluperfect subjunctive formed?
questions.hint: Pluperfect subjunctive: hubiera/hubiese estudiado (had studied - subjunctive form).

questions.question: How is conditional perfect formed?
questions.hint: Conditional perfect: habría aprobado (would have passed).

questions.question: 'Como llegues tarde, te quedarás sin postre' - What does COMO express?

answers.text: Warning/threat (if you arrive late - strong warning)

questions.hint: COMO + subjunctive = warning/threat. If you (dare) arrive late, consequences! More forceful than si.

questions.question: 'Como no estudies, suspenderás' - What mood after COMO?
questions.hint: COMO + subjunctive for warnings. Como no estudies (subjunctive) = If you don't study (warning).

questions.question: 'De tener tiempo, iría contigo' means...

answers.text: If I had time, I would go with you (formal/literary)
From having time, I would go with you
To have time, I would go with you
Of time, I would go with you

questions.hint: DE + infinitive = formal alternative to si clause. De tener = Si tuviera (If I had).

questions.question: 'De haberlo sabido, no habría venido' - What does DE express?
questions.hint: DE + perfect infinitive = formal 'if' for past hypotheticals. De haberlo sabido = Si lo hubiera sabido.

questions.question: 'Con más dinero, viajaría más' - Where is the condition?
questions.hint: Implied condition. Con más dinero = (Si tuviera) más dinero (If I had more money).

questions.question: 'En tu lugar, yo no iría' - What condition is implied?

answers.text: If I were in your place (but I'm not)

questions.hint: Implied condition: En tu lugar = Si yo estuviera en tu lugar (If I were in your place).
